receipt.public_excerpt: ChatGPT's paid subscribers surpassed 20 million, up from 15.5 million at the end of 2024, according to The Information.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms the 15.5 million paid subscriber input. Dividing it by the top of his 500-600 million MAU range gives 2.583%, so the conditional arithmetic is correct.

inputs: 600 million monthly active users (speaker's upper estimate)

receipt.public_excerpt: "Insane thing: We are currently losing money on OpenAI Pro subscriptions!" he wrote in a post.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI's CEO confirmed that at least one group of paying users, the $200 Pro tier, cost more to serve than it paid. This supports the claim for that tier only.

metric_scope.metric: Profit or loss on ChatGPT Pro subscriptions

receipt.public_excerpt: an internal figure measuring the share of revenue after the costs of running models for paying users of its corporate and consumer products. As of October, OpenAI’s compute margins reached 70%, up from 52% at the end of 2024

evidence_items.explanation: At the end of 2024, about 52% of paying-user revenue reportedly remained after the cost of running models for those users. That means paying users as a group brought in more than it cost to serve them, which contradicts 'every single user, regardless of whether they pay, loses the company money'.

metric_scope.metric: Compute margin on paying users (revenue minus model-running costs for paying users, as share of revenue)

unresolved_gaps: OpenAI does not publish monthly active users, so the real conversion rate cannot be checked; only his arithmetic can be.
The compute margin figure comes from an unnamed source and OpenAI declined to confirm it.
No public per-user figure exists that includes training and overhead costs, which a broader reading of 'loses money' would need.
